summary.text: An 84-year-old patient with arterial hypertension, dyslipidemia and a previous transient ischemic attack on aspirin presented to the emergency department with a GCS of 14, disorientation and right-sided hemiparesis. Cranial MRI revealed bilateral chronic subdural hematoma, and bilateral 2 burr-hole trephination with subgaleal drains was followed by uneventful recovery and discharge to a geriatric rehabilitation facility, neurologically intact.

One month later new gait disturbance and cognitive decline appeared and CT showed recurrent bilateral CSH; the burr holes were reopened bilaterally with subgaleal drains and the patient went home on postoperative day 5 with complete resolution of symptoms. Three months after the index surgery a mild left upper-limb motor drift and progression of the right-sided hematoma led to a third, right-sided surgery with adjunctive navigated soMMA, discharge on postoperative day 4 and reintroduction of aspirin.

Follow-up for 8 months postoperatively found no recurrence or neurological deficits, and the case table lists a full recovery outcome. Figure 3 shows a 3D CT reconstruction of this patient with the navigated pterional burr hole covered by a titanium plate, positioned at the pterional MMA sulcus.

summary.text: An 85-year-old patient with recurrent vertebrobasilar ischemic strokes on clopidogrel, COPD (GOLD stage 2), chronic kidney disease and arterial hypertension presented to the emergency department with a GCS of 14, impaired gait and generalized weakness without lateralization. Cranial CT showed a left-sided CSH, and left-sided 2 burr-hole trephination with a subgaleal drain was followed by uneventful recovery and discharge home on postoperative day 4.

Two weeks later he returned with new-onset slurred speech, a GCS of 14 and a residual left-sided CSH; revision through the previous burr holes with a subgaleal drain led to discharge home after 6 days without residual deficits. Two weeks later worsening gait instability and aphasia with persistent left-sided residual hematoma prompted a third revision with subgaleal drainage and adjunctive navigated soMMA, and clopidogrel was resumed.
Clinical and radiological follow-up continued for 11 months after the index procedure with no evidence of recurrence or neurological deficits, and the case table lists a full recovery outcome.

summary.text: A 79-year-old patient with cardiac arrhythmia, congenital epilepsy, mitral valve insufficiency and a mechanical aortic valve, on long-term phenprocoumon (INR 2.4 on admission), was referred with headache, gait disturbance, bilateral lower limb weakness and aphasia. Cranial CT revealed bilateral CSH with mass effect.

Anticoagulation was reversed preoperatively with prothrombin complex concentrate and vitamin K, and bilateral burr-hole trephination with subgaleal drainage was performed. Recovery was favorable with complete resolution of deficits, the patient was transferred on postoperative day 3 neurologically intact, and subtherapeutic LMWH was started. Ten days after the initial surgery a symptomatic recurrent left-sided hematoma with mass effect led to revision with navigated soMMA; LMWH was later increased and bridged back to phenprocoumon.
Follow-up for 3 months after the index procedure found no recurrence or neurological symptoms, and the case table lists a full recovery outcome.

summary.text: An 83-year-old patient with a history of myocardial infarction treated with coronary stenting, extracranial carotid artery stenosis, a previous transient ischemic attack and a recent mild traumatic brain injury, on ongoing clopidogrel therapy, presented with preserved consciousness (GCS 15), progressive headache and gait and balance disturbance. Cranial MRI revealed bilateral CSH.

Bilateral burr-hole trephination with subgaleal drains was followed by uneventful recovery and discharge to a geriatric rehabilitation facility. Twenty days postoperatively renewed gait disturbance and ataxia with recurrence of the left-sided CSH led to revision with re-evacuation and a subgaleal drain, and discharge to rehabilitation after 3 days with improved gait. Clopidogrel was resumed; 3 months after the index procedure vertigo and worsening gait with a recurrent left-sided CSH led to revision with subgaleal drainage and navigated soMMA through a pterional burr hole.

The patient was discharged home on postoperative day 8 with improved gait and no residual ataxia, and follow-up 5 months after the initial surgery confirmed a stable condition without neurological deficits; the case table lists a full recovery outcome. Figures 2 and 4 show the CT bone window with a visible MMA sulcus and the 3D CT position of the pterional burr hole.
